cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet in Judah, gets a word from the LORD about a drought. Judah mourns, her gates languish, and a cry goes up from Jerusalem. Friend, this is not a 'we're out of sprinkles' kind of morning.

cards.question: In the drought, the nobles send their servants to the cisterns for water. What do the servants find there?

cards.text: The jars come back EMPTY. All that walking, and I bet those empty jars felt heavier on the way home.

cards.question: The servants' jars come back empty. Ashamed and humiliated, what do they do?

cards.text: Out in the countryside, it's no better. The farmers look down at their fields, and the ground is cracked.

cards.question: In Judah, the ground is cracked because no ___ has fallen on the land.
Looking at the cracked ground, the farmers are ashamed and cover their heads too.

cards.text: Then even the animals feel it. The doe in the field deserts her newborn fawn.

cards.question: In the drought, why does the doe in the field desert her newborn fawn?

cards.text: Wild donkeys stand on the barren heights, panting for air like jackals. Friend, I haven't breathed that hard since I chased a runaway chocolate chip across my whole counter.

cards.question: Up on the barren heights, the wild donkeys find plenty of pasture.

cards.text: Then the voice changes. A prayer goes up to the LORD, and it doesn't make excuses: "our iniquities testify against us."

cards.question: In the prayer to the LORD, they admit their rebellions are ___.
Even with their sins testifying against them, what do they ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Act for the sake of His name
Send them a brand new king

cards.text: They call Him the Hope of Israel, and ask why He's like a stranger, like a traveler who stays but a night. You know the type: crashes on your couch and he's GONE before you wake up.
Then they ask why He's like a man taken by surprise, like a warrior powerless to save. That's a HARD question to bring to God, and they bring it anyway.

cards.question: Even after all those hard questions, what does the prayer say is still true about the LORD?
The prayer in the drought ends by asking the LORD not to forsake them.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks about this people: "Truly they love to wander; they have not restrained their feet."

cards.question: Because the people love to wander, the LORD accepts them and forgets their iniquity.
Instead of forgetting this people's iniquity, what does the LORD say He will now do?

answers.text: Remember it and punish their sins
Wait and see what they do next
Send them one more warning first

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Jeremiah himself, with a word just for him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Jeremiah not to do?

answers.text: Speak to the king of Judah
Weep for this people in secret

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah that if the people fast, He will listen to their cry.
The people may bring burnt offerings and grain offerings. What does the LORD say He'll do with them?

cards.text: Jeremiah replies, "Ah, Lord GOD!" Then he points to what the other prophets are telling the people.

cards.question: What are the other prophets telling the people of Judah?

cards.text: The LORD answers Jeremiah about those prophets. And He doesn't soften it one bit.

cards.question: The LORD says the prophets promising peace are telling the truth in His name.

cards.text: He says He did not send them, appoint them or speak to them. That's somebody signing YOUR name on a card you never even saw.

cards.question: The LORD says the false prophets' vision is the delusion of their own ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about the prophets He didn't send, the ones who say, 'No sword or famine will touch this land.'

cards.question: How does the LORD say those very prophets will meet their end?

cards.text: And it doesn't stop with the prophets. The LORD turns to the people they prophesy to.

cards.question: The people who listen to those prophets will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem with no one to bury them.

cards.text: Not them, their wives, their sons or their daughters. The LORD says, "I will pour out their own evil upon them."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "our iniquities testify against us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Armed guards" is a different kind of thing from "No water" and "Muddy water," which both describe the water. It stands out and is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Story card 10 and the question itself say the donkeys stand on "barren heights." That rules out "plenty of pasture" before the baker reasons about it, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks what is "still true about the LORD" after hard questions. The right answer is the only positive one. Both wrong answers are negative ("gone far away," "forgotten them"), and the framing excludes them.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke "crashes on your couch and he's GONE before you wake up" plays the prayer's picture of God for laughs and makes God the flaky houseguest. The humor lands on God rather than on a human situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: No card tells the LORD's words in 14:12, "I will finish them off by sword and famine and plague." This is the LORD's own verdict, and it sets up the contrast with the prophets' promise that the people "will not see the sword or suffer famine" (14:13, 15). It is an important detail that is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Story card 10 says the LORD "doesn't soften it one bit." That tells the baker the LORD's answer about the prophets is harsh, which rules out "True" (that they tell the truth in His name) before the baker reasons about it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says "The people who listen to those prophets." The text says "the people to whom they prophesy" (14:16). The text never says these people listen, so the card adds a detail that isn't in the passage.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
